arch-body-hold.name: Arch Body Hold
steps: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight and together.
Squeeze your glutes and back, lifting arms, chest and legs off the floor at the same time.
Hold an even curve like an upturned boat, eyes on the floor.
Breathe steadily, hold 10–30 seconds, then lower and rest.
safety: Keep your neck in line with your spine; do not tilt your head back.
If you feel sharp lower-back pain, reduce the height or go back to the superman.

arch-hang.name: Arch Hang
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip and straight arms.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, pushing your chest toward the bar so your upper back arches.
Hold the position with abs braced and legs still.
Build up hold time to about 20–30 seconds per set.
safety: Keep your arms straight at all times; do not shrug.
Come down slowly; do not just let go and drop.

archer-pull-up.name: Archer Pull-Up
steps: Grip the bar overhand very wide, about twice shoulder width, and hang with straight arms.
Pull your chin toward one hand, bending only that arm; the other arm stays straight and pushes along the bar.
Lower back to the hang with control.
Switch sides; to make it easier, rest the assisting hand on top of the bar.
safety: Do the same number of reps on both sides.
Stop if the elbow of the straight arm hurts.

archer-push-up.name: Archer Push-Up
steps: Place your hands very wide, about twice shoulder width, body straight.
Shift your weight to one side and bend that elbow to lower yourself, keeping the other arm straight out to the side.
Lower until your chest is close to the bending hand.
Push back to center, then switch sides on the next rep.
safety: Only train this once you can do many clean standard push-ups.
Do not twist your torso or shift your hips to compensate.

archer-row.name: Archer Row
steps: Lie under the bar and grip it very wide.
Pull yourself toward one hand, keeping the other arm straight as a support.
Pull until your chest nearly touches the bending hand, shoulder blades squeezed together.
Lower with control, then switch sides.
safety: Keep the assisting arm straight at all times; do not turn it into a two-arm row.
Keep your torso from twisting.

assisted-knee-copenhagen-plank.name: Assisted Knee Copenhagen Plank
steps: Lie on your side next to a low bench, propped on your elbow (or hand) under your shoulder.
Place the inner side of your top knee on the bench; the bottom leg stays on the floor.
Lift your hips so your body is straight, with the bottom leg supporting only as much as needed.
Hold for the planned time, then lower and switch sides.
safety: Do not let your hips sag; use as little help from the bottom leg as possible.
Stop if you feel sharp groin pain; this exercise loads the adductors heavily.

assisted-squat.name: Assisted Squat
equipment: post or door frame to hold on to
steps: Stand facing a sturdy post, door frame or chair back and hold it with both hands.
Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Sit down as deep as you can, using your hands only as much as needed.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall; gradually use less arm help over sessions.
safety: Knees track in the direction of your toes; do not let them cave in.
The support must be fixed and not slip.

bench-dip.name: Bench Dip
steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench with your hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips off the bench, legs extended in front (bend your knees to make it easier).
Bend your elbows to lower until your upper arms are nearly parallel to the floor, elbows pointing straight back.
Straighten your elbows to push yourself up.
safety: Do not go too deep: the shoulders get pushed forward, which can easily cause shoulder joint pain.
Keep your back close to the bench edge and your chest open.

bicycle-crunch.name: Bicycle Crunch
steps: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your head, legs lifted with knees bent to 90°.
Contract your abs to lift your head and shoulders off the floor.
Extend one leg while rotating your torso to bring the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Alternate sides in a pedaling rhythm, steady and controlled.
safety: Rotate from your torso; do not yank your neck with your hands.
Keep a moderately slow pace; going too fast lets momentum replace the muscles.

bird-dog.name: Bird Dog
steps: Start on all fours: hands directly under shoulders, knees directly under hips, back flat.
Brace your abs and extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back at the same time.
Hold arm, torso and leg in a straight line for 1–2 seconds.
Return to the start, then switch sides.
safety: Do not rotate your hips or arch your back when lifting the leg.
Raise the leg only to torso level, no higher.

bodyweight-calf-raise.name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, hands on a wall for balance.
Press evenly through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a beat at the top.
Lower your heels slowly with control, then repeat.
safety: Do not let your ankles roll out or in on the way up.
Lower slowly; do not bounce your heels.

bodyweight-curl.name: Bodyweight Curl
steps: Hold the rings or suspension straps facing the anchor point and lean back until the straps are taut, arms straight, palms up.
Raise your elbows to shoulder height or higher and keep them fixed.
Bend your elbows to pull yourself toward your hands, hands traveling toward your forehead.
Straighten your arms to lower slowly; walk your feet forward to make it harder.
safety: The anchor point must be able to hold your full body weight.
Keep your body straight like a plank; do not push your hips up.

bodyweight-hammer-curl.name: Bodyweight Hammer Curl
steps: Hold the rings with palms facing each other and lean back until your arms are straight.
Raise your elbows high and keep them still.
Bend your elbows to bring your fists toward your temples.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.
safety: Keep your wrists straight; do not curl your wrists to pull.
Start with your body nearly upright before leaning back further.

bodyweight-romanian-deadlift.name: Bodyweight Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, hands on your stomach or hanging at your sides.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes to keep your lower back flat.
Push your hips back and tip your torso forward with only a slight knee bend, until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up in one smooth movement.
safety: Keep your back straight; you can hold a stick along your back to check yourself.
Do not try to bend lower than you can with a straight back.

bodyweight-squat.name: Bodyweight Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms reaching forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, pushing the knees out in the direction of your toes.
Sit as deep as you can while your heels stay on the floor and your back stays straight.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up until hips and knees are fully extended.
safety: Do not let your knees cave in on the way down or up.
Heels lifting is a sign of stiff ankles: reduce the depth and work on ankle mobility.

bodyweight-triceps-extension.name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
steps: Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width and walk your feet back so your body leans in a straight line like a standing plank; the higher the bar, the easier, the lower, the harder.
Keep your arms straight, abs and glutes tight.
Bend your elbows and let your head drop below the bar, upper arms staying nearly still.
Straighten your elbows to push back to the start.
safety: Start with a high bar to reduce the load on your elbows.
Move slowly; do not drop at the bottom.

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
steps: Stand with your back to a knee-height bench, about one long stride away.
Rest the top of your rear foot on the bench; keep your feet about hip-width apart side to side.
Lower yourself with control until the back knee nearly touches the floor, torso upright.
Drive through the front foot to stand up; switch legs after the set.
safety: Do not let the front knee cave in.
The back leg is only for balance; do not push off the bench with it.

chin-up.name: Chin-Up
steps: Grip the bar underhand (palms facing you), shoulder-width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades down and lift your chest.
Bend your elbows to pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
safety: Do not jerk your body or swing your legs.
Stop if the inside of your elbow hurts; a slightly wider grip may feel better.

clamshell.name: Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to about 90°, legs stacked.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and lightly brace your abs.
Keeping your feet together, open the top knee as high as you can without your hips rolling back.
Lower the knee slowly back to the start; switch sides after the set.
safety: The top hip must stay still; do not roll your body back.
If it is too easy, switch to side-lying leg raises instead of forcing range of motion.

close-grip-push-up.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
steps: Get into a push-up position but with hands exactly shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Keep your body straight with abs lightly braced.
Lower yourself with elbows tucked close to your ribs and pointing back.
Push up until your elbows are fully extended.
safety: Do not let your elbows flare out; if your elbows hurt, widen your hands slightly.
Keep your wrists stacked under your shoulders.

commando-pull-up.name: Commando Pull-Up
steps: Stand under the bar, turned to face along it; grip with hands close together, one in front of the other, palms facing each other.
Hang, brace your abs and glutes, and pull your shoulder blades down.
Bend your elbows to pull up, moving your head to one side of the bar until your shoulder nearly touches the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight; on the next rep, bring your head to the other side.
safety: Only train this once you can do many standard pull-ups.
Do not kick your legs or twist your body for momentum; stop if your elbows hurt.

copenhagen-plank.name: Copenhagen Plank
steps: Lie on your side, propped on your elbow under your shoulder, with the ankle or foot of your top leg on the bench.
Brace your abs and lift your lower hip so your body is straight from shoulders to feet.
Let the bottom leg hang under the bench or only lightly touch it.
Hold for the full time, or lower your hips slowly and raise them again for the dynamic version; then switch sides.
safety: Only progress to the long-lever version once you can solidly hold the knee version for 3×30 seconds.
If you feel knee or groin pain, go back to the knee version.

copenhagen-plank-with-movement.name: Copenhagen Plank with Movement
steps: Get into a long-lever Copenhagen plank with the top foot resting on the bench.
Keeping your hips high, pull the bottom knee up toward your chest.
Extend the bottom leg back to the neutral position with control.
Repeat for the planned reps, then switch sides.
safety: Do not let your hips sag while the bottom leg moves.
The load on the adductors is very high; increase volume gradually to avoid groin pain.

cossack-squat.name: Cossack Squat
steps: Stand with feet wide apart, torso upright.
Bend one knee and lower yourself deep toward that leg; the other leg stays straight out to the side, toes pointing up.
Keep the foot of the bent leg flat on the floor.
Drive through the heel of the bent leg to stand up, then switch to the other side.
safety: Only go as deep as you can with your heel on the floor and your back not rounding.
You can hold on to a post in the early stages.

crunch.name: Crunch
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent about 90°, feet on the floor, arms crossed over your chest.
Contract your abs and curl your head and shoulders off the floor, as if bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Curl up only while your lower back still touches the floor, then pause for a beat.
Lower slowly, keeping your abs tight, then do the next rep.
safety: Do not pull your neck with your hands; look diagonally up at the ceiling to keep your neck straight.
Keep your lower back on the floor at all times; do not swing your whole torso up with momentum.

dead-bug.name: Dead Bug
steps: Lie on your back with arms straight up toward the ceiling; bend hips and knees to 90° so your shins are parallel to the floor.
Brace your abs, press your lower back lightly into the floor and keep it there for the whole set.
Slowly extend one leg out low over the floor while bringing the opposite arm back overhead.
Bring arm and leg back to the start, then switch sides; breathe steadily, do not hold your breath.
safety: If your lower back starts lifting off the floor, shorten the range of the leg extension.
Move slowly; do not swing your arms and legs for momentum.

dead-hang.name: Dead Hang
steps: Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
Lift your feet to hang fully, arms straight.
Try hanging with relaxed shoulders, then actively pull the shoulders down to feel the difference.
Hold for time, increasing it gradually each session.
safety: Come down onto your feet; do not let go while hanging high.
Keep a box under your feet if you cannot hang for long yet.

decline-push-up.name: Decline Push-Up
steps: Place your toes on a bench or box and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width.
Brace your abs so your body is straight from head to heels, without piking at the hips.
Lower your chest toward the floor with control.
Push up until your arms are straight; raise the foot height gradually as you adapt.
safety: The box under your feet must be sturdy and not slip.
The higher your feet, the more load on the shoulders; progress gradually.

deficit-tibialis-raise.name: Deficit Tibialis Raise
steps: Stand with your heels on the edge of a low step, the front of your feet hanging off.
Keeping your body straight, let your toes drop as low as possible.
Pull your toes up as high as you can, feeling the muscle on the front of your shin.
Hold for a beat, then lower slowly and repeat.
safety: Stand close to a wall or handrail so you do not fall backward.
Use a low, stable step.

diamond-push-up.name: Diamond Push-Up
steps: Get into a push-up position with your hands under your chest, thumbs and index fingers touching to form a diamond.
Keep your body straight like a plank, shoulder blades down.
Lower your chest toward your hands, elbows tucked close to your body.
Push up until your arms are straight; if it is too hard, place your hands slightly narrower than normal and bring them closer over time.
safety: Stop if your wrists or elbows hurt; turning your hands slightly outward may help.
Do not let your hips sag when fatigued.

donkey-kick.name: Donkey Kick
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Brace your abs and keep your back flat.
Keeping the knee bent at 90°, push one heel up toward the ceiling, squeezing your glutes.
Lower the leg without touching the floor, repeat, then switch sides.
safety: Do not arch your back or rotate your hips to kick higher.
Put a pad under your knees if the floor is hard.

dragon-flag.name: Dragon Flag
steps: Lie on your back on a bench, hands gripping the edge of the bench firmly behind your head.
Raise your legs and torso until only your shoulders rest on the bench, body straight from shoulders to feet.
Keeping a hollow body, lower your whole body very slowly until your back is close to the bench.
Pause for a beat, then raise back to the start.
safety: Do not pike at the hips or sag at the lower back; if you cannot hold a straight body yet, train the tucked version or negatives only.
The bench must be sturdy and not tip over.

eccentric-heel-drop.name: Eccentric Heel Drop
steps: Stand on the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, holding a wall or handrail.
Rise onto your toes with both feet.
Lift one foot and lower the heel of the other very slowly, below the edge of the step.
Put the other foot back down, rise again with both feet and repeat.
safety: The step must be stable and dry; always have something to hold on to.
Make the lowering phase last 2–3 seconds; do not drop your heel.

elevated-pike-push-up.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
steps: Place your feet on a bench or box and walk your hands close to it so your hips are above your shoulders and your torso is nearly vertical.
Brace your abs, hands slightly wider than shoulder width.
Bend your elbows to lower your head to the floor in front of your hands, elbows tucked at an angle.
Push up until your arms are straight; raise the height gradually once you reach 3×8–12.
safety: The box must be sturdy and not slip.
Lower slowly with control; do not let your head hit the floor.

elevated-pike-shrug.name: Elevated Pike Shrug
steps: Place both feet on a box and walk your hands toward it so your hips are bent about 90°, shoulders directly over your hands, arms straight.
Brace your abs and keep your elbows straight throughout.
Let your shoulders sink down, moving slightly away from your ears.
Push the floor away, shrugging your shoulders toward your ears so your body rises a few centimeters; hold for a beat, then lower with control.
safety: Warm up your wrists first; do not bend your elbows when shrugging.
Stop if you feel dizzy or your shoulders hurt; bring your feet down to the floor to rest.

false-grip-hang.name: False Grip Hang
steps: Set the rings at head height and wrap your hands over the rings so each ring sits under your wrist, knuckles pointing up.
Flex your wrists tightly, lift your feet to hang, arms straight and shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abs and glutes to avoid swinging, shoulders slightly depressed.
Hold for time, then bend your knees and put your feet down before letting go.
safety: Keep your wrists on top of the rings; letting them slip down reduces the effect and makes injury more likely.
Keep sessions short at first, since the skin and wrists need time to adapt.

false-grip-ring-row.name: False Grip Ring Row
steps: Grip the rings with a false grip and lean back until your arms are straight.
Keeping your body straight, pull the rings toward your chest while keeping your wrists flexed.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.
Readjust your grip after each rep if it slips; walk your feet back to make it easier.
safety: Increase intensity gradually, since this exercise puts heavy stress on the wrists and skin.
Use chalk or grip tape if your hands are slippery.

feet-elevated-side-plank.name: Feet-Elevated Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side next to a low bench or box, bottom elbow directly under your shoulder.
Rest both feet, stacked, on top of the bench.
Brace your abs and lift your hips off the floor until your body is straight from head to feet.
Hold 10–30 seconds, then lower and switch sides.
safety: Only train this once you can hold a regular side plank for about 30 seconds.
The bench must be stable and not slip.

fingertip-push-up.name: Fingertip Push-Up
steps: Get into a push-up position, supported on the tips of all five spread fingers, fingers held stiff and slightly bent.
Brace your abs, body straight.
Lower your chest with control, without your fingers collapsing.
Push up; if it is too hard, do it on your knees first.
safety: You need to be proficient at regular push-ups; progress slowly and do not train to failure.
Stop immediately if your finger joints hurt.

fire-hydrant.name: Fire Hydrant
steps: Start on all fours, eyes on the floor.
Lightly brace your abs and, keeping the knee bent, lift one leg out to the side using your glutes.
Lift only as high as your glutes stay contracted and your torso does not tilt.
Lower the leg slowly and repeat; then switch sides.
safety: Do not lean to the other side to lift the leg higher.
Lower the leg with control.

flexed-arm-hang.name: Flexed-Arm Hang
steps: Place a box under the bar and grip the bar at shoulder width.
Step up on the box so your chin is above the bar, elbows fully bent and tucked close to your body.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears, brace your abs, then lift your feet off the box and hold.
Hold 10–30 seconds, then lower slowly or step back down onto the box.
safety: Do not drop when fatigued; always come down with control.
Do not hold your breath or crane your neck to keep your chin above the bar.

front-lever.name: Front Lever
steps: From a tuck front lever, press your arms down hard using your lats.
Gradually extend both legs until your whole body forms a straight line parallel to the floor.
Keep your hips from piking, shoulder blades pulled down, elbows straight.
Hold a few seconds, then tuck your knees back to the tuck position before lowering.
safety: Progress through advanced tuck and one-leg front lever first; each stage can take many months.
Avoid piking at the hips to cheat.

full-can-raise.name: Full Can Raise
steps: Stand tall, arms at your sides, thumbs pointing forward (like holding a full can).
Move your arms about 30° forward of straight out to the side.
Raise your straight arms to shoulder height without shrugging.
Lower slowly to the start.
safety: Stop at shoulder height if going higher causes pain.
Do not turn your thumbs down (empty-can style) to avoid shoulder impingement.

glute-bridge.name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Tuck your pelvis slightly to engage your glutes.
Drive your hips up with your glutes until shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a beat, then lower slowly.
safety: Push with your glutes; do not arch your lower back to lift your hips higher.
If your hamstrings cramp, bring your feet closer to your glutes.

hamstring-slide.name: Hamstring Slide
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on a towel/sliders and lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Slide your heels away with control, keeping your hips from dropping.
Contract your hamstrings and glutes to pull your heels back toward your glutes while your hips stay up.
Repeat the extend–curl sequence for the planned reps.
safety: If your hips drop partway, go back to the eccentric-only (extension) version.
Place your hands beside your body for stability if needed.

hanging-knee-raise.name: Hanging Knee Raise
steps: Jump up to grab the bar and hang with straight arms, feet off the ground.
Pull your shoulders down slightly and brace your abs so your body does not swing.
Bend your knees and pull your thighs up as high as possible in front of you.
Pause for a beat, then lower your legs slowly; pause briefly at the bottom before the next rep.
safety: Do not swing for momentum; pause briefly at the top and bottom of each rep.
If your arms are tired and you are about to slip, get down immediately, landing on both feet.

hanging-leg-raise.name: Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from the bar with straight arms, legs together and straight.
Hold a hollow body, keeping your legs in front of your hips at all times so you do not swing.
Raise both straight legs to at least hip height, as high as you can.
Lower your legs slowly with control, then repeat.
safety: First train the bent-knee version and the straight-leg negatives until solid.
Do not swing your legs; if you start swinging hard, come to a full stop at the bottom before continuing.

hanging-windshield-wiper.name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
steps: Hang from the bar with straight arms, legs together.
Brace your abs and raise your straight legs to at least hip height (higher if you can).
Keeping your legs straight, rotate slowly to one side until you are close to losing control.
Bring your legs through the middle to the other side; repeat for the planned reps, then lower your legs.
safety: Only train this once you can do clean straight-leg hanging leg raises for 3×8.
Control the range of motion; do not fling your legs for momentum; get off the bar immediately when your arms tire.

heel-walk.name: Heel Walk
steps: Stand tall.
Lift your toes and the balls of your feet so only your heels touch the ground.
Walk forward on your heels for a set distance or time.
Keep your toes pulled up the whole way, then rest.
safety: Walk on a flat, non-slippery surface.
Take short steps to keep your balance.

hip-hitch.name: Hip Hitch
steps: Stand on one leg on a step or low box, the other leg hanging off the edge; touch a wall for balance.
Keeping both knees straight, slowly lower the hip on the hanging side so that foot drops below the step.
Use the hip of the standing leg to pull your pelvis back up, slightly higher than level.
Repeat slowly; switch sides after the set.
safety: The movement comes from the hip; do not bend the knee or lean your torso.
Use a low, stable box; always have something to hold on to.

hollow-body-hold.name: Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and arms extended overhead.
Press your lower back into the floor and brace your abs.
Lift your legs about 15–30° off the floor while raising your head, shoulders and arms so your body curves like a boat.
Hold the position, breathing steadily; only your lower back and glutes touch the floor.
When time is up, lower your legs, shoulders and head to rest.
safety: Your lower back lifting off the floor means it is too hard: bend your knees or bring your arms closer to your body to make it easier.
Do not hold your breath during the hold.

incline-push-up.name: Incline Push-Up
steps: Place your hands on the edge of a sturdy bench, box or table, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight like a plank, abs lightly braced.
Lower your chest toward the edge, elbows pointing diagonally back.
Push up until your arms are straight; once you reach 3×8, lower the hand surface.
safety: Check that the bench/box does not slip before training.
Keep your neck in line with your body; do not jut your head forward.

inverted-row.name: Inverted Row
steps: Set the bar at hip height (or lower the rings), lie under the bar and grip it overhand slightly wider than shoulder width, heels on the floor.
Brace your abs and glutes so your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then pull your chest to the bar, elbows tucked.
Lower with control until your arms are straight.
safety: Do not let your hips sag or thrust your hips up to cheat.
Raise the bar if you cannot yet pull your chest to it.

isometric-neck-extension.name: Isometric Neck Extension
steps: Sit or stand tall, looking straight ahead, neck in a neutral position.
Interlace your hands and place them behind your head.
Press your head back into your hands while your hands resist, so the head does not move.
Hold about 6–10 seconds, rest briefly, repeat 8–12 times.
safety: Do not use maximum effort; increase force gradually without causing pain.
Do not tilt your head back while pressing; breathe steadily.

isometric-neck-flexion.name: Isometric Neck Flexion
steps: Sit tall with your head in a neutral position.
Place your palm on your forehead.
Push your head forward into your hand while the hand holds still, so the neck does not move.
Hold 10 seconds, relax, repeat 3 times.
safety: Increase force gradually without causing pain.
Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath.

isometric-neck-lateral-flexion.name: Isometric Neck Lateral Flexion
steps: Sit tall, head neutral.
Place your palm on the temple on one side.
Push your head sideways into your hand, the hand holding still so the neck does not move.
Hold 10 seconds, switch sides, 3 times per side.
safety: Do not rotate or drop your head while pushing.
Stop if pain radiates down into your arm.

isometric-shoulder-abduction.name: Isometric Shoulder Abduction
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, upper arm against your body, elbow bent 90°.
Press the outside of your elbow or forearm against the wall.
Push your arm out sideways into the wall without shrugging, so the joint does not move.
Hold 5–10 seconds, repeat 10 times.
safety: Start with light force and increase gradually without pain.
Do not lean your torso to push.

isometric-shoulder-external-rotation.name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
steps: Stand next to a wall or door frame, elbow bent 90° and tucked against your body.
Place the back of your wrist against the wall, wrist straight.
Push the back of your hand outward into the wall as if rotating your forearm out, so the joint does not move.
Hold 5–10 seconds, starting at about 20% effort and increasing gradually.
safety: Use moderate force without causing pain.
Keep your shoulders relaxed; do not shrug.

isometric-shoulder-internal-rotation.name: Isometric Shoulder Internal Rotation
steps: Stand in a door frame, elbow bent 90° and tucked against your body.
Place your palm on the edge of the door frame in front of your stomach.
Press your palm inward as if pulling your hand toward your stomach, so the joint does not move.
Hold 5–10 seconds, increasing force gradually from light to moderate.
safety: It should not cause pain; reduce the force if uncomfortable.
Keep your wrist straight.

isometric-wrist-extension.name: Isometric Wrist Extension
steps: Sit with your forearm resting on a table or your thigh, palm down, wrist slightly extended.
Place your other hand on the back of the working hand.
Press down with the top hand while the bottom hand holds still, so the wrist does not move.
Hold for a while with moderate force, rest, then repeat; increase hold time gradually over sessions.
safety: Use moderate force; pain should not increase after training.
Keep the elbow bent and the forearm supported.

jackknife-sit-up.name: Jackknife Sit-Up
steps: Lie on your back, arms extended overhead, legs straight.
Brace your abs, then lift your legs and upper body at the same time, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Come up until your body forms a V shape and pause briefly.
Lower slowly without letting your arms and legs touch the floor, then do the next rep.
safety: Lower with control; do not drop your back onto the floor.
If your lower back feels uncomfortable, go back to lying leg raises or bend your knees as you fold up.

knee-copenhagen-plank.name: Knee Copenhagen Plank
steps: Lie on your side next to a low bench, propped on your elbow under your shoulder.
Place the inner side of your top knee on the bench.
Lift your hips until your body is straight, lifting the bottom leg off the floor (let it hang under the bench).
Hold for the planned time, then lower and switch sides.
safety: Keep your hips high; do not rotate your torso forward.
You can support yourself on your hand instead of your elbow if that is more comfortable for your shoulder.

kneeling-back-of-hand-wrist-push-up.name: Kneeling Back-of-Hand Wrist Push-Up
steps: Start on all fours with the backs of your hands on the floor, fingers pointing toward your knees.
Let your weight rest lightly on the backs of your hands, wrists flexed.
Extend your wrists to lift your forearms, then lower slowly.
Repeat 5–10 times; shift your body back to make it easier.
safety: Keep the load light at first; the wrists need time to adapt.
Stop if you feel sharp pain on the back of the wrist.

kneeling-palm-pulse.name: Kneeling Palm Pulse
steps: Start on all fours, palms flat on the floor under your shoulders, fingers spread.
Keeping your fingers pressed into the floor, lift the heels of your hands so your weight shifts onto your fingers.
Lower the heels of your hands slowly.
Repeat 5–20 times; shift your body forward to increase the load.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in the wrist or finger joints.
Warm up with wrist circles first.

kneeling-plank.name: Kneeling Plank
steps: Rest both forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders, both knees on the floor.
Lift your hips so your head, back and hips form a straight line.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes, holding the position for the planned time.
Lower your hips to rest and repeat; once you can hold 3×30 seconds, move on to the standard plank.
safety: Do not let your hips sag or pike up.
End the set when you can no longer keep your body straight.

kneeling-side-plank.name: Kneeling Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side, propped on your elbow directly under your shoulder, knees bent and stacked.
Lift your hips so your head, torso and knees form a straight line.
Brace your abs and hold the position for the planned time.
Lower your hips to rest, then switch sides.
safety: Push the floor away so your shoulder does not sink into your neck.
Do not let your hips drop or rotate forward.

l-sit.name: L-Sit
steps: Sit on the floor with legs straight, hands beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Tighten your quads, brace your abs and lock your arms straight.
Press hard into the floor to lift your hips and legs, legs parallel to the floor.
Keep your shoulders depressed and your back from rounding; when time is up, lower down.
safety: Only raise your legs as high as you can while keeping them straight and your back from rounding.
Train on the floor first; use low parallel bars or handles if your wrists feel uncomfortable.

l-sit-pull-up.name: L-Sit Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Raise both straight legs in front of you to hip height (L shape); if too hard, bend your knees.
Holding the L, pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower with control, legs still level.
safety: You need strict pull-ups and a hanging L hold before training this.
Do not arch your lower back or let your legs drop for momentum.

lying-leg-raise.name: Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lie on your back, arms along your sides, legs straight and together.
Brace your abs and raise both legs until your toes point at the ceiling.
Lower your legs very slowly, stopping just before they touch the floor.
Repeat without letting your lower back arch up.
safety: If your lower back lifts off the floor, bend your knees slightly or only lower your legs halfway.
Do not swing your legs for momentum.

lying-neck-curl-bodyweight.name: Lying Neck Curl (bodyweight)
steps: Lie on your back on a bench with your head off the edge.
Tuck your chin slightly and keep it tucked throughout the set.
Flex your neck to bring your chin toward your chest, shoulders staying on the bench.
Pause for a beat, then slowly lower your head back to the start.
safety: Lower your head with control; do not let it drop.
Do not lift your shoulders to compensate.

lying-neck-extension-bodyweight.name: Lying Neck Extension (bodyweight)
steps: Lie face down on a bench with your head off the edge, feet on the floor for stability.
Tuck your chin slightly, neck in a neutral position.
Raise your head by extending your neck, the back of your head moving toward the ceiling.
Pause for a beat, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not overextend your neck at the top.
Lower with control.

lying-windshield-wiper.name: Lying Windshield Wiper
steps: Lie on your back with arms spread out to the sides and both straight legs raised toward the ceiling.
Brace your abs and slowly lower your legs to one side, keeping them together.
Stop when the opposite shoulder is about to lift off the floor, then pull your legs back to center.
Lower to the other side and repeat.
safety: Do not let your legs drop freely; if you cannot control them yet, go back to the bent-knee version.
Keep both shoulders pressed to the floor at all times.

lying-windshield-wiper-bent-knees.name: Lying Windshield Wiper with Bent Knees
steps: Lie on your back with arms spread out to the sides to stabilize your torso, legs lifted with knees bent 90°.
Brace your abs and slowly tilt both knees to one side, shoulders staying on the floor.
Stop before the opposite shoulder lifts, then pull your knees back to center.
Continue tilting to the other side; each side counts as one rep.
safety: Lower your legs slowly, only as far as you can still control.
People with lumbar disc problems should reduce the range of rotation.

mountain-climber.name: Mountain Climber
steps: Get into a push-up position, hands shoulder-width apart, back straight, abs braced.
Drive one knee toward your chest as close as you can.
Return that leg to the start while bringing the other knee up.
Keep alternating legs, keeping your hips low and your back flat.
safety: Do not let your hips pike up or sag as you speed up.
If your wrists hurt, support yourself on your fists or push-up handles.

muscle-up.name: Muscle-Up
steps: Grip the bar with a false grip (wrists flexed, knuckles on top of the bar) and hang with straight arms.
Pull very hard, bringing the bar toward your stomach on a curved path rather than pulling straight up.
At the transition, lean your chest over the bar and drive your elbows back and up.
Press your arms straight as in a dip to get on top of the bar, then lower with control.
safety: You need a solid base of pull-ups and dips before training this; practice with jumping from a box or negatives first.
The way down is hard to control: train over a mat and avoid free-falling.

negative-chin-up.name: Negative Chin-Up
steps: Place a box under the bar and grip the bar underhand at shoulder width.
Step up so your chin is over the bar, elbows bent, shoulder blades pulled down.
Lift your feet off the box and lower yourself very slowly (about 3–5 seconds) until your arms are fully straight.
Step back onto the box and repeat.
safety: Do not drop at the end of the lowering phase; keep your shoulders active as your arms near straight.
Increase the lowering time gradually; stop if your elbows or wrists hurt.

negative-dip.name: Negative Dip
steps: Use a box or jump up into a support position on the parallel bars, arms straight.
Lower yourself very slowly, counting 5–10 seconds, elbows tucked and pointing back.
Stop when your shoulders drop below your elbows or at a comfortable depth.
Put your feet down, step back up and repeat.
safety: Control the entire lowering phase; do not drop at the end.
Increase reps gradually, since slow negatives cause a lot of muscle soreness.

negative-hamstring-slide.name: Negative Hamstring Slide
steps: Lie on your back with your heels on a towel or sliders on a smooth floor, arms along your sides.
Lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Keeping your hips high, slowly slide your heels away until your glutes touch the floor or your knees are fully straight.
Lower your hips, bring your legs back to the start in the easiest way, then repeat.
safety: Keep your pelvis neutral; do not arch your back.
Slide slowly and evenly; stop if your hamstrings cramp.

negative-pull-up.name: Negative Pull-Up
steps: Stand on a box, grip the bar overhand, and jump or step up so your chin is over the bar.
Hold for a beat at the top, chest toward the bar.
Lower yourself very slowly, counting 5–10 seconds, until your arms are straight.
Step back onto the box and repeat.
safety: Do only 2–3 sets the first time, since the lowering phase causes a lot of muscle soreness.
Do not drop at the end, to avoid jerking your elbows and shoulders.

neutral-grip-pull-up.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
steps: Grip two parallel handles (or both sides of an H-shaped bar) with palms facing each other, shoulder-width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades down, chest up.
Bend your elbows to pull yourself up until your chin clears the handles.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
safety: Check that the handles are secure before hanging.
Do not use leg momentum.

nordic-curl.name: Nordic Curl
equipment: foot anchor or a partner holding your feet
steps: Kneel with your ankles hooked securely under a fixed object about a fist's width above the ankle.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips extended, body straight.
Lower yourself slowly forward without bending at the hips.
From the lowest point, use your hamstrings to pull your torso back up to upright kneeling.
safety: Only train this once you can do clean negatives or the band-assisted version for 3×8.
Do not bend at the hips to cheat; stop if you feel pain behind the knee.

nordic-hamstring-eccentric.name: Nordic Hamstring Eccentric
equipment: foot anchor or a partner holding your feet
steps: Kneel on a pad with hips extended, ankles hooked under a fixed object or held by a partner.
Squeeze your glutes so your body is straight from knees to head.
Lean forward by extending your knees, using your hamstrings to brake so you go down very slowly.
When your chest is close to the floor, catch yourself with your hands and push gently back to kneeling.
safety: Do not push your hips back; the movement must happen at the knee joint.
Always be ready to catch yourself with your hands; increase reps gradually, as this exercise causes a lot of muscle soreness.

one-arm-dead-hang.name: One-Arm Dead Hang
steps: Hang from the bar with both hands, then gradually shift your weight onto one hand.
Let go with the other hand and engage the hanging shoulder (pull it down slightly).
Hold a few seconds, limiting body rotation.
Grip with both hands again before coming down.
safety: Start with very short hangs, shoulder active.
Only relax the shoulder once you are strong enough.

one-arm-pull-up.name: One-Arm Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with one hand, the other arm relaxed or behind your back; brace your abs and glutes and keep your legs together.
Pull the shoulder blade of the hanging arm down into an active hang.
Bend your elbow to pull yourself up, keeping your body from rotating, until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly with control to a straight arm, then switch hands.
safety: Only train this once you are solid at archer pull-ups and assisted one-arm pull-ups; increase reps gradually.
Do not drop at the end of the lowering phase, to avoid overloading the elbow and shoulder.

parallel-bar-dip.name: Parallel Bar Dip
steps: Support yourself on the parallel bars, arms straight, shoulders depressed.
Bend your elbows to lower yourself, elbows pointing back, torso leaning slightly forward.
Lower until your shoulders are below your elbows or as far as your mobility allows.
Push up until your arms are fully straight and your shoulders pressed down.
safety: Do not shrug your shoulders to your ears at the bottom; build training volume gradually, as this exercise stresses the shoulders and sternum.
Do not swing for momentum.

parallel-bar-support-hold.name: Parallel Bar Support Hold
steps: Grip both parallel bars and jump or step up to support yourself on straight arms.
Press your shoulders down away from your ears, elbow pits facing forward.
Keep your legs together, glutes squeezed, body straight or slightly hollow.
Hold 20–60 seconds, building up to 3 sets of 1 minute.
safety: Do not let your shoulders shrug up to your ears; if you cannot hold, lightly touch your feet down on a box.
You can use two sturdy chairs instead of parallel bars.

pike-push-up.name: Pike Push-Up
steps: From a push-up position, walk your feet toward your hands and push your hips up high into an inverted V.
Hands slightly wider than shoulder width, head relaxed in line with your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands, elbows at about 45° to your body.
Push back to the V position; once you reach 8–10 clean reps, move on to the feet-elevated version.
safety: Do not let your hips drop, or the exercise turns into a regular push-up.
Do not flare your elbows straight out to the sides, to protect your shoulders.

pistol-squat.name: Pistol Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight out in front, both arms reaching forward.
Bend the knee of the standing leg and lower yourself, keeping the extended leg off the floor.
Go as deep as you can while keeping your balance and your heel on the floor.
Drive through the heel of the standing leg to stand up; switch legs after the set.
safety: Train a partial range (sitting down onto a box) before going all the way down.
Lower slowly; do not drop into the bottom.

planche-lean.name: Planche Lean
steps: Place your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers turned outward, arms straight, elbow pits facing forward.
Protract your shoulder blades, squeeze your glutes and abs, in a push-up position.
Slowly lean your shoulders forward past your hands, arms still straight.
Hold for time, breathing steadily; stop when your form starts to break down.
safety: Warm up your wrists thoroughly and increase the lean bit by bit.
Do not bend your elbows or let your hips sag.

plank.name: Plank
steps: Rest your forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders, legs straight and supported on your toes.
Brace your abs as if about to be punched in the stomach and squeeze your glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Push the floor away with your forearms so your shoulders do not sink.
Keep breathing steadily until time is up; build up gradually to 30 seconds per set.
safety: Do not let your lower back sag, especially when fatigued.
Stop as soon as your form starts to break down instead of forcing a few more seconds.

plank-back-of-hand-wrist-push-up.name: Plank Back-of-Hand Wrist Push-Up
steps: Get into a straight-arm plank with the backs of your hands on the floor, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Brace your abs, body straight.
Extend your wrists to lift your forearms, pushing your body up slightly, then lower slowly.
Do only a few reps, prioritizing control.
safety: Only train this once the wall version is easy.
Put a soft mat under your hands; stop if the back of your wrist hurts.

plank-palm-pulse.name: Plank Palm Pulse
steps: Get into a straight-arm push-up position, palms flat under your shoulders.
Press your fingers into the floor and lift the heels of your hands to push your body up onto your fingers.
Lower the heels of your hands slowly; you can do only the slow lowering phase at first.
Keep your body straight throughout the set.
safety: Only move on to this version once the kneeling version feels easy.
Do not let your hips sag.

prone-neck-bridge.name: Prone Neck Bridge
steps: Kneel in front of a padded bench and rest your forehead on the pad.
Keep your back straight, hands on your thighs or the bench for balance.
Press your forehead lightly into the pad.
Flex and extend your neck through small, controlled ranges.
safety: Keep the range small; do not roll your head.
Use your hands to take some of the load when starting out; stop if you feel numbness or radiating pain.

prone-t-raise-bodyweight.name: Prone T Raise (bodyweight)
steps: Lie face down with arms out to the sides in a T, thumbs pointing to the ceiling.
Initiate by squeezing your shoulder blades toward your spine.
Raise both arms as high as you can, arms straight.
Hold a few seconds, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not arch your lower back to lift higher.
Easier version: work one arm at a time, or lie on the edge of a bed so the arm moves through a shorter range.

prone-w-raise.name: Prone W Raise
steps: Lie face down with elbows bent about 90°, upper arms close to your body, forming a W shape.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and pull them down.
Rotate your forearms and lift your elbows and the backs of your hands off the floor, thumbs pointing up.
Hold 2 seconds, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not shrug or tilt your neck back.
Keep your chin tucked, eyes on the floor.

prone-y-raise-bodyweight.name: Prone Y Raise (bodyweight)
steps: Lie face down on the floor or a bed, forehead resting on a towel, arms extended overhead in a Y, thumbs pointing up.
Tuck your chin slightly and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Lift both arms a few centimeters off the floor, leading with your thumbs.
Hold 2 seconds, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not shrug or tilt your neck back.
Work one arm at a time or reduce the range if your shoulder hurts.

pseudo-planche-push-up.name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
steps: Get into a push-up position with your hands turned outward or fingers pointing toward your feet, hands placed beside your hips.
Lean forward until your shoulders are past your hands, keeping your body straight and your shoulder blades protracted.
Keeping the same lean, bend your elbows to lower your chest close to the floor, elbows tucked.
Push up until your arms are straight; increase the lean to make it harder.
safety: Warm up your wrists thoroughly; increase the lean gradually.
Keep the lean constant throughout each rep and do not let your hips sag.

pull-up.name: Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, body in a slight hollow.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, then bend your elbows to pull your chest up toward the bar.
Pull until your chin clears the bar or the bar touches your upper chest.
Lower with control until your arms are fully straight.
safety: Do not kick your legs for momentum if you want to train the right muscles.
Your grip should not be too wide; use chalk if your hands are slippery.

push-up.name: Push-Up
steps: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, toes on the floor, body straight from head to heels.
Brace your abs and glutes, pulling your shoulder blades down away from your ears.
Lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the floor, elbows tucked diagonally back.
Push the floor away to straighten your arms; at the top, push a little further so your shoulder blades spread apart.
safety: Do not let your hips sag or pike up; if you cannot keep your body straight, go back to the incline version.
If your wrists hurt, support yourself on your fists or push-up handles to keep your wrists straight.

push-up-plus.name: Push-Up Plus
steps: Get into a standard push-up position, hands shoulder-width apart, body straight.
Lower yourself as far as is pain-free, then push up until your elbows are nearly straight.
At the top, push the floor further so your shoulder blades spread apart, upper back slightly rounded.
Let your shoulder blades return to neutral, then do the next rep.
safety: Do not let your lower back sag or round your back excessively during the scapular push.
Do the hands-elevated version if you cannot keep your body straight yet.

reverse-grip-bodyweight-curl.name: Reverse-Grip Bodyweight Curl
steps: Grip the rings or a bar set at chest height with an overhand grip (backs of the hands facing up).
Lean back until your arms are straight, elbows raised to shoulder height.
Bend your elbows to pull yourself toward your hands, keeping your wrists straight.
Lower slowly; stand more upright if you cannot keep your wrists straight.
safety: Stand nearly upright when starting out, since the overhand grip is weaker.
Stop if the outside of your elbow hurts.

reverse-hyperextension-bodyweight.name: Reverse Hyperextension (bodyweight)
steps: Lie face down on a bench or sturdy table with the edge at hip level and your legs hanging down.
Hold both sides of the bench firmly, brace your abs and tuck your pelvis slightly.
Squeeze your glutes to raise both straight legs to torso level.
Pause for a beat, then lower your legs slowly.
safety: Keep your pelvis tucked; do not fling your legs too high and arch your lower back.
The bench/table must be sturdy enough and not slip.

reverse-lunge.name: Reverse Lunge
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step back with one leg.
Lower yourself deep, the back knee coming close to but not touching the floor.
Drive through the front foot to bring the back leg back to standing; alternate legs or finish one side first.
safety: Keep your torso upright; do not lean forward.
Do not slam your back knee into the floor.

reverse-nordic.name: Reverse Nordic
steps: Kneel on a pad with your torso upright and the tops of your feet flat on the floor.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips extended.
Bend at the knees and lean your whole body back as one straight unit from knees to head.
Lean back as far as you can still control, then use your quads to pull yourself back upright.
safety: Start with a short range; this exercise is very demanding on the knees.
Do not bend at the hips or arch your back to lean further.

ring-ab-rollout.name: Ring Ab Rollout
steps: Set the rings low at hip height, grip them and walk your feet back so your body leans like a push-up.
Lock your elbows and hold a hollow body: ribs down, glutes squeezed.
Push the rings forward, gradually bringing your arms overhead so your body lowers.
Go as far as you can while keeping your body straight, then pull your arms back to the start.
safety: The higher the rings, the easier; start high and lower them gradually.
Your lower back sagging is a sign it is too hard: shorten the range.

ring-dip.name: Ring Dip
steps: Support yourself on the rings, arms straight, rings turned out.
Bend your elbows to lower yourself, keeping the rings close to your body and your shoulders depressed.
Lower until your shoulders are below your elbows or to a comfortable depth.
Push up, turning the rings out again at the top.
safety: Only train this once you are solid on parallel bar dips; the unstable rings greatly increase the load on the shoulders.
Increase training volume gradually so your shoulders and sternum can adapt.

ring-push-up.name: Ring Push-Up
steps: Lower the rings to a few centimeters off the floor, grip them and get into a push-up position with straight arms.
Keep the rings close to your sides, shoulder blades down, body straight.
Lower yourself until your hands are about level with your chest, elbows tucked in.
Push up; at the top, turn the rings slightly out and protract your shoulder blades.
safety: Check that the straps and anchor point are secure before training.
Do not let the rings drift wide to the sides, which can easily overload the shoulders.

ring-reverse-fly.name: Ring Reverse Fly
steps: Set the rings at chest height and grip them with palms facing each other, arms straight out in front.
Walk your feet forward and lean back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels, abs and glutes tight.
Keeping a slight bend in the elbows, open your arms out to the sides until they are in line with your shoulders, pulling your body up.
Lower yourself slowly along the same path; stand more upright to make it easier, lean back more to make it harder.
safety: Do not shrug or arch your back for momentum; do not let your hips sag.
Start nearly upright and only increase the lean while you can maintain technique.

ring-support-hold.name: Ring Support Hold
steps: Set the rings at hip height, grip them and jump up to a straight-arm support.
Keep the rings tight against your hips, shoulders pressed down, elbow pits facing forward.
Once stable, turn your thumbs outward so the rings turn out (RTO) as much as possible.
Hold in short sets, building up gradually to 60 continuous seconds.
safety: You can wrap a resistance band or towel between the rings for support when starting out.
Do not rest your arms against the straps, as this hides your true strength.

scapula-dip.name: Scapula Dip
steps: Support yourself on the parallel bars, arms straight, legs slightly forward, abs and glutes tight.
Relax so your shoulders shrug up toward your ears while your elbows stay straight.
Press both hands down into the bars, pulling your shoulders down away from your ears to raise your body a few centimeters.
Hold for a beat, then lower with control.
safety: Keep your elbows straight at all times; the movement is only at the shoulder blades.
Reduce the range if you feel sharp shoulder pain.

scapular-pull-up.name: Scapular Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades down and together so your shoulders move away from your ears and your body rises a few centimeters.
Hold for a beat, elbows still straight.
Let your shoulder blades return to the hanging position with control.
safety: Do not bend your elbows: this is a shoulder blade exercise.
If you cannot hang for long yet, let your feet lightly touch a box.

shrimp-squat.name: Shrimp Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other knee bent behind you (you can hold that ankle with the same-side hand).
Lower yourself on the standing leg, torso leaning slightly forward for balance.
Lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor (easier version: back knee and toes touch at the same time).
Drive through the standing leg to stand up; switch legs after the set.
safety: Place a soft pad under the back knee.
The knee of the standing leg tracks over the toes; do not let it cave in.

side-lunge.name: Side Lunge
steps: Stand tall with space clear to one side, abs lightly braced.
Take a wide step to one side.
Lower yourself toward the stepping leg, pushing your hips back, the other leg straight; keep the heel of the stepping foot on the floor.
Drive through the stepping foot to push back to standing; repeat or switch sides.
safety: Prioritize control over depth.
The knee of the stepping leg tracks over the toes.

side-lying-external-rotation.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
steps: Lie on your side with the top elbow bent 90°, upper arm against your ribs (you can hold a rolled towel there).
Pull your shoulder blade back and down.
Rotate your forearm up toward the ceiling, elbow staying still and bent at 90°.
Lower slowly to the start.
safety: Keep your elbow against your ribs; keep your shoulder blade still.
Do not swing your arm; lower more slowly than you lift.

side-lying-hip-abduction.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
steps: Lie on your side, bottom leg bent for stability, top leg straight in line with your body.
Brace your abs and keep your pelvis vertical (not tilting forward or back).
Raise the top leg, leading with the heel, toes pointing slightly down.
Hold for a beat at the top, then lower slowly; switch sides after the set.
safety: Do not rotate your torso or bring the leg forward to lift higher.
Keep the top knee straight throughout.

side-lying-hip-adduction.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
steps: Lie on your side, head resting on your bottom arm, top hand on your hip.
Cross the top leg over in front and place that foot on the floor in front of the bottom leg.
Exhale and raise the bottom leg (straight) a few centimeters.
Lower slowly; switch sides after the set.
safety: Stop if your hips tilt or you feel strain in your lower back.
A small range is enough; do not rotate the leg to lift higher.

side-lying-hip-hike.name: Side-Lying Hip Hike
steps: Lie on your side with both knees bent; you can squeeze a soft pillow between your knees.
Keep your lower back neutral and lightly brace your abs.
Contract the muscles along your side to pull the top hip up toward the same-side shoulder, without your torso rolling forward or back.
Slowly return to the start; do 10–15 reps, then switch sides.
safety: Keep the movement small; do not tense your neck or shoulders.
Stop if your lower-back pain increases.

side-lying-neck-lateral-raise.name: Side-Lying Neck Lateral Raise
steps: Lie on your side on a bench with your shoulder at the edge so your head can move freely.
Look straight ahead; do not rotate your head.
Lower your head slowly until you feel a light stretch, then raise your ear toward your top shoulder.
Switch sides after each set.
safety: Only tilt in a single plane; do not combine it with flexing, extending or rotating.
Move slowly; do not jerk.

side-plank.name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side, propped on your elbow directly under your shoulder, legs straight (place the top foot in front of the bottom foot for stability).
Brace your abs and lift your hips so your body is straight from head to heels.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, for the planned time.
Lower to rest, then switch sides.
safety: Do not let your hips sag; if too fatigued, go back to the kneeling version.
If the supporting shoulder hurts, stop and recheck your elbow position.

side-plank-hip-abduction.name: Side Plank with Hip Abduction
steps: Get into a side plank: elbow under shoulder, legs straight and stacked, hips raised high.
Keep shoulders, hips, knees and ankles in line.
Raise the top leg slowly and lower it slowly, without the bottom hip dropping.
Do the planned reps, then switch sides.
safety: Easier version: bend the bottom knee about 45° and support yourself on that knee.
Stop when your hips start to sag.

side-plank-lift.name: Side Plank Lift
steps: Lie on your side with the bottom forearm on the floor, elbow directly under your shoulder, legs straight and stacked.
Brace your abs and glutes so your body is straight.
Lift your hips into a side plank and hold for a beat.
Lower your hips until they lightly touch the floor, then lift again; do 10–15 reps, then switch sides.
safety: Do not drop your hips; lower with control.
If your shoulder or lower back hurts, switch to the kneeling version.

single-leg-calf-raise.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
steps: Stand on one leg on the floor with the other leg bent up, hand on a wall.
With the knee of the standing leg straight, raise your heel as high as possible.
Keep pressure even across the ball of your foot, without rolling toward the big toe or little toe.
Lower the heel slowly and repeat; switch legs after the set.
safety: Your hand is only for balance; do not pull yourself up with it.
If your Achilles tendon hurts, reduce the reps and go back to the two-leg version.

single-leg-deficit-calf-raise.name: Single-Leg Deficit Calf Raise
steps: Stand on the ball of one foot on the edge of a step, the other leg bent behind you, holding on to something.
Lower your heel slowly to below the level of the step and pause for a beat.
Push up as high as possible with the knee straight, pausing for a beat at the top.
Repeat; switch legs after the set.
safety: Lower slowly so the Achilles tendon is not jerked.
Place your foot securely on the edge of the step and do not let it slip.

single-leg-glute-bridge.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot on the floor, the other leg straight (or pulled up toward your chest).
Tuck your pelvis slightly and brace your abs.
Drive through the heel of the working leg to lift your hips until your body is straight.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, keeping both hips level, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not let the hip on the straight-leg side drop.
Push with your glutes; do not arch your back.

single-leg-hamstring-slide.name: Single-Leg Hamstring Slide
steps: Lie on your back with one heel on a towel/slider, the other leg lifted or resting on the working leg.
Lift your hips using the working leg.
Slide the heel away and then pull it back toward your glutes, keeping your hips up and level at all times.
Do the planned reps, then switch legs.
safety: Do the single-leg eccentric-only (extension) version first if you cannot pull back in yet.
Do not let your hips rotate or drop to one side.

single-leg-hip-thrust.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a sturdy bench or sofa.
Place one foot on the floor and lift the other leg.
Drive through the heel of the working leg to push your hips up until your torso is parallel to the floor and the working knee is bent about 90°.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips slowly.
safety: The bench must not slip; ideally place it against a wall.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and do not arch your lower back at the top.

single-leg-romanian-deadlift.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand on one leg, the standing knee slightly bent, abs braced.
Hinge at the hip, tipping your torso forward while the other leg extends back in line with your torso.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstring of the standing leg, with both hips still level.
Drive your hips forward to stand up; do 5–8 reps, then switch legs.
safety: If you lose balance, lightly touch the back toes to the floor or hold on to a wall.
Keep your back straight; do not rotate the hip of the lifted leg open.

soleus-raise.name: Soleus Raise
steps: Stand on one leg with a hand on a wall, the standing knee slightly bent.
Keeping the same knee bend, raise your heel as high as possible.
Pause for a beat at the top.
Lower the heel slowly, knee still bent; switch legs after the set.
safety: Do not straighten your knee as you raise your heel, or the exercise shifts to the gastrocnemius.
Lower with control.

split-squat.name: Split Squat
steps: Step one foot forward a long stride, back heel raised; hold this stance for the whole set.
With your torso upright, lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand up, without bringing your feet together between reps.
Do the planned reps, then switch legs.
safety: The front knee tracks over the toes.
Keep your feet about hip-width apart side to side for easier balance.

standing-ab-wheel-rollout.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bend over and place the ab wheel on the floor in front of your toes.
Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, hold a hollow body and push the wheel away.
Roll until your body is nearly parallel to the floor (or until you touch a wall placed in front to limit the range).
Pull the wheel back using your abs and shoulders, returning to the bent-over start position.
safety: Only train this after you can do clean kneeling rollouts; use a wall to shorten the rolling distance.
Do not let your lower back sag; if you lose position, drop to your knees immediately.

standing-hip-flexion-hold.name: Standing Hip Flexion Hold
steps: Stand tall next to a wall with one hand touching it for balance.
Lightly brace your abs and raise one thigh forward to about 30–60°, knee comfortably bent.
Hold the thigh at that height for 10–30 seconds without leaning your torso back.
Lower the leg and switch sides; when it gets easy, gradually raise the thigh higher, up to 90°.
safety: Keep your back straight; do not arch your lower back to lift the thigh higher.
If the front of your hip hurts, reduce the lift angle.

step-up.name: Step-Up
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench about knee height.
Place your whole foot on the box and shift your weight onto the top leg.
Lightly brace your abs and drive through the top leg to stand up tall, minimizing push from the bottom leg.
Lower slowly with control, keeping the foot on the box, and repeat.
safety: The box must not slip or tip over.
Start with a lower box if your knee is not yet stable.

superman.name: Superman
steps: Lie face down, arms extended forward, legs extended back, tops of the feet on the floor.
Look down at the floor to keep your neck straight; brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Exhale and lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor a few centimeters at the same time.
Pause for a beat, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not tilt your neck back to look up.
Only lift a few centimeters; lifting too high compresses the lower back.

supine-neck-bridge.name: Supine Neck Bridge
steps: Lie on your back so that only the back of your head rests on the bench, feet on the floor, knees bent.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your body straight.
Press the back of your head lightly into the bench.
Nod your head through small, controlled ranges.
safety: The bench version is easier and safer than the floor version; do not do the floor version until you are used to it.
Stop if you feel dizzy, numb or radiating pain.

supine-straight-leg-raise.name: Supine Straight Leg Raise
steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot on the floor, the other leg straight.
Tighten the quads of the straight leg to lock the knee.
Raise the straight leg to the height of the bent knee and hold for a beat.
Lower slowly to near the floor and repeat; after all reps, switch sides.
safety: Keep your lower back on the floor with the help of the bent leg.
Lower the leg with control; do not let it drop.

towel-pull-up.name: Towel Pull-Up
steps: Drape two strong towels over the bar and grip one tightly in each hand.
Hang with straight arms, shoulder blades down.
Pull yourself up as high as you can, keeping your hands squeezing the towels.
Lower with control until your arms are straight.
safety: Use thick towels that are not frayed; check that the towels do not slide off the bar.
Only train this once you can do many clean regular pull-ups.

tuck-front-lever.name: Tuck Front Lever
steps: Hang from the bar or rings with straight arms.
Press your arms down with your lats, lean back and tuck your knees to your chest so your torso is horizontal.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, elbows fully straight.
Hold 10–30 seconds, then lower your legs with control.
safety: Do not bend your elbows to compensate; bent elbows reduce the effect and make pain more likely.
Do not hang upside down for more than a second at the start or end of a set.

tuck-front-lever-row.name: Tuck Front Lever Row
steps: Get into a tuck front lever on the rings or bar, arms straight.
Keeping your body horizontal, pull the rings toward your stomach, shoulder blades squeezed together.
Bring the rings to touch your lower torso if you can.
Extend your arms back to the tuck front lever with control.
safety: Only train this once you can solidly hold a tuck front lever for 20–30 seconds.
Rings allow better range of motion than a bar; do not let your hips drop when fatigued.

tuck-l-sit.name: Tuck L-Sit
steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent about 90°, hands placed slightly in front of your hips.
Lock your elbows and press your shoulders down (do not shrug them to your ears).
Push the floor away to lift your hips and feet, keeping your knees tucked close to your body.
Hold 10–30 seconds, then lower down to rest.
safety: If your wrists hurt, support yourself on your fists or on two low handles.
If you cannot lift your feet yet, go back to the support version with your feet still touching the floor.

tuck-planche.name: Tuck Planche
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor beside your hips, fingers turned outward.
Lean your shoulders forward, protract your shoulder blades and round your back slightly.
Lift your feet off the floor, knees tucked to your chest, hips at shoulder level.
Hold a few seconds with straight arms, then put your feet down.
safety: You need a solid planche lean first; you can use low handles to reduce wrist stress.
Do not bend your elbows to hold the position, as this can easily overload the biceps tendon.

underhand-inverted-row.name: Underhand Inverted Row
steps: Lie under a bar at hip height and grip it underhand at shoulder width.
Keep your body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest toward the bar, elbows tucked close to your body.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
safety: Do not jerk your body; keep your hips in line.
Stop if the inside of your elbow hurts.

vertical-row.name: Vertical Row
steps: Grip a bar or rings at chest height, feet placed almost directly below your hands, body leaning back slightly.
Pull your shoulder blades back first, then pull your chest toward your hands.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Lower back to straight arms with control; walk your feet forward to make it harder.
safety: Check that the anchor point or bar is secure.
Do not shrug as you pull.

wall-angel.name: Wall Angel
steps: Stand with your back, head and hips against the wall, feet a few centimeters from the wall; gently press your lower back toward the wall.
Raise your arms into a goalpost position: backs of the hands, wrists and elbows touching the wall, elbows bent 90°.
Slide your arms up overhead while keeping contact with the wall.
Slide down until your elbows come close to your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
safety: Shorten the range if your arms come off the wall or your lower back arches.
Go slowly, about 3 seconds up and 3 seconds down.

wall-back-of-hand-wrist-push-up.name: Wall Back-of-Hand Wrist Push-Up
steps: Stand facing a wall with the backs of your hands on the wall, fingers pointing down.
Lean into the wall so your weight rests on the backs of your hands.
Extend your wrists to push yourself away from the wall, then lower slowly.
Move your hands gradually lower on the wall to increase the load.
safety: Keep your elbows nearly straight; do not push with your shoulders.
Increase the difficulty a little at a time.

wall-handstand-hold.name: Wall Handstand Hold
steps: Walk up the wall (wall walk) into a handstand, facing the wall, toes lightly touching it.
Arms straight, push the floor away so your shoulders rise toward your ears.
Squeeze your abs and glutes so your body is straight, without arching your lower back.
Hold for time, then walk your hands out to come down.
safety: Work on mobility and warm up your wrists before training.
Train on a mat and learn how to bail out safely before holding for long.

wall-handstand-push-up.name: Wall Handstand Push-Up
steps: Get into a wall handstand (facing the wall), hands shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abs and keep your body straight.
Bend your elbows to slowly lower your head close to the floor, elbows tucked diagonally forward.
Push up until your arms are fully straight.
safety: You need a solid 30–45 second wall handstand hold before training this.
Lower slowly and have a mat under your head; do not flare your elbows out to the sides.

wall-handstand-shoulder-tap.name: Wall Handstand Shoulder Tap
steps: Walk up the wall into a handstand facing the wall, arms straight and shoulder-width apart, hands a short distance from the wall.
Squeeze your abs and glutes so your body forms a straight line, pushing the floor away to keep your shoulders high.
Gradually shift your weight onto one hand, keeping your body from shifting, then lift the other hand to lightly tap the same-side shoulder.
Put the hand back on the floor, regain balance, then switch sides; do a few reps per side, then walk your hands out to come down.
safety: Only train this once you can hold a wall handstand for about 30 seconds and know how to bail out safely.
Do not let your hips pike or your lower back arch when shifting weight; train on a mat and stop when the supporting arm starts to bend.

wall-handstand-shrug.name: Wall Handstand Shrug
steps: Get into a wall handstand (walking up the wall or kicking up), arms straight and shoulder-width apart.
Squeeze your abs and glutes so your body is straight.
Let your shoulders sink down, moving slightly away from your ears, arms still straight.
Push the floor away, shrugging your shoulders toward your ears to raise your body as high as possible; repeat rhythmically, then come down safely.
safety: Only train this once you can hold a wall handstand for about 30 seconds and know how to bail out.
Do not bend your elbows or let your lower back arch; train on a mat.

wall-push-up.name: Wall Push-Up
steps: Stand about an arm's length from a wall and place your palms on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lightly brace your abs and glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest close to the wall; elbows at about 45° to your body, not flared out.
Push the wall away to straighten your arms back to the start, exhaling as you push.
safety: Do not let your hips sag or stick your butt out.
Step your feet further from the wall once 3×8 is easy, then move on to incline push-ups.

wall-push-up-plus.name: Wall Push-Up Plus
steps: Stand facing a wall with both hands on the wall at shoulder height, arms straight.
Keep your body straight from heels to the top of your head.
Without bending your elbows, let your shoulder blades slide toward your spine so your chest moves slightly toward the wall.
Push the wall away with your shoulder blades so your upper back widens and your chest moves away from the wall.
safety: Keep your elbows straight at all times.
Do not shrug your shoulders to your ears as you push.

wall-slide.name: Wall Slide
steps: Stand facing a wall with the outer edges of both forearms on the wall, elbows bent about 90° at shoulder height.
Press your forearms lightly into the wall and gently protract your shoulder blades.
Slide your forearms up in a V shape, letting your shoulder blades rotate upward naturally.
Slide back to the start with control.
safety: Do not shrug or arch your lower back as your arms go overhead.
Stop within a pain-free range.

wall-tibialis-raise.name: Wall Tibialis Raise
steps: Stand with your back to a wall, heels about 20–30 cm from the wall.
Lean your back and glutes against the wall, abs lightly braced, legs straight.
Pull your toes up as high as possible, heels staying on the floor.
Hold 1–2 seconds, then lower your toes slowly.
safety: Keep your heels on the floor at all times.
Lower slowly; do not let your toes slap down.

wall-walk.name: Wall Walk
steps: Get into a push-up position with the soles of your feet against the base of the wall.
Walk your feet up the wall step by step while walking your hands back toward the wall.
Stop at a distance close to the wall that you can still control, and hold for a beat.
Reverse: hands walk forward, feet come down, back to the push-up position.
safety: Clear the area, use a mat, and train barefoot or in grippy shoes.
Walk only a short distance at first, then increase gradually.

wide-row.name: Wide Row
steps: Lie under the bar and grip it overhand about 1.5 times shoulder width (on rings, keep your elbows flared about 90°).
Keep your body straight, abs braced.
Pull your chest up to the bar, elbows flaring out to the sides, shoulder blades fully squeezed together.
Lower with control until your arms are straight.
safety: Do not shrug your shoulders to your ears.
Lower your feet if you cannot reach the bar.

wrestlers-bridge.name: Wrestler's Bridge
steps: Lie on your back on a thick mat, knees bent, feet on the floor wider than hip width; place both hands beside your head, elbows pointing up.
Push your hips up high and, supporting yourself with your hands, slowly roll onto the top of your head.
Keep most of your weight on your feet and hands, squeezing your glutes to keep your hips high; the neck takes only a light load.
Hold a few seconds, then use your hands to lower your back to the mat; increase hold time very gradually over many weeks.
safety: Do not train this if you have a history of neck pain, a herniated disc or neck injury; consult a medical professional first.
Always train on a mat or pad and keep your hands supporting you until you are very stable; do not roll your head or take your hands away without a coach.
Stop immediately if you feel dizzy, numb or pain radiating into the shoulders or arms.
